question.problem:
Given that $2a≡2b\,(\text{mod}\,8),$ which of the following statements **must** be true?

- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,6)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,4)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,8)$
question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

We're asked to consider the following statement:

$$
2a≡2b\,(\text{mod}\,8)
$$

Notice that $\text{gcd}(2,8)=2.$

Applying the division property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2a & ≡2b &  & (\text{mod}\,8) \\ 2\cdot a & ≡2\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,2\cdot 4) \\ \cancel{2}\cdot a & ≡\cancel{2}\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{2}\cdot 4) \\ a & ≡b &  & (\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

$$
{{field-1}}a≡{{field-2}}b\,(\text{mod}\,{{field-3}})

question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

In our case, we have a common factor of $k=3,$ and the congruence can be written as

$$
3\cdot 3a≡3\cdot 3b\,(\text{mod}\,3\cdot 5).
$$

Therefore, we can cancel out the common factor on both sides of the congruence and the modulus:

$$
\cancel{3}\cdot 3a≡\cancel{3}\cdot 3b\,(\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 5)\,⟺\,3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,5)
$$

- $2a≡2b\,(\text{mod}\,3)$
- $3a≡3b\,(\text{mod}\,6)$
- $a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,9)$
question.worked_solution:
The division property of modular arithmetic states that for $k\ne 0,$ we have

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

We're asked to consider the following statement:

$$
6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,9)
$$

Notice that $\text{gcd}(6,9)=3.$

Applying the division property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6a & ≡6b &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ 3\cdot 2\cdot a & ≡3\cdot 2\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 3) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot 2\cdot a & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot 2\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 3) \\ 2a & ≡2b &  & (\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,kn)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

$$
ka≡kb\,(\text{mod}\,n)\,⟺\,a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. Applying the first property, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3a & ≡3b &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ 3\cdot a & ≡3\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,3\cdot 3) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot a & ≡\cancel{3}\cdot b &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{3}\cdot 3) \\ a & ≡b &  & (\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is true. By statement I and the second property, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,3)\,⟺\,4a≡4b\,(\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
